q-ows.label: One word for a phrase
q-ows.summary: A phrase is given; pick the single word that means the same.

rules.text: Many one-word substitutions are built from a Greek or Latin root: phobia (fear), phile (lover), mis(o) (hate), anthropo (mankind). Match the root to the phrase.
rules.ok: Bibliophile: biblio (book) + phile (lover) = lover of books.
rules.bad: Bibliophobe is not the word for a lover of books; phobe means one who fears.

q-ows.cue: 'Select the word that can be used as a substitute for the given group of words.'
q-ows.standard: Know the word, or break it into root parts and match them to the phrase.
q-ows.fast: Split each option into its root, discard the roots that do not match the phrase.
q-ows.eliminate: The wrong options are usually real words with a neighbouring meaning (hater instead of lover), so match both halves of the root.
traps: A word with the right root but the opposite sense (phile vs phobe).
A word that sounds similar but belongs to another phrase.

practice.text:
Select the word that can be used as a substitute for the given group of words.
One who knows everything
practice.why: Omniscient is built from omni (all) and scient (knowing): one who knows everything.

a.note: Omnipotent means all-powerful: it shares the root omni but not the sense of knowing.

c.note: Omnipresent means present everywhere, not knowing everything.

d.note: A philanthropist is a person who loves mankind and helps others.

practice.text:
Select the word that can be used as a substitute for the given group of words.
One who hates mankind
practice.why: Misanthrope joins miso (hate) and anthropos (man): one who hates mankind.

a.note: Philanthropist has the same anthropo root but phil means love, so it is the opposite sense.

b.note: A bibliophile is a lover of books.

d.note: A somnambulist is one who walks in sleep.

practice.text:
Select the word that can be used as a substitute for the given group of words.
A lover of books

b.note: A misanthrope hates mankind; it has nothing to do with books.

c.note: Illegible describes writing that cannot be read; it is an adjective, not a person.

d.note: Omniscient means knowing everything, not loving books.

practice.text:
Select the word that can be used as a substitute for the given group of words.
One who walks in sleep
practice.why: Somnambulist comes from somnus (sleep) and ambulare (walk).

a.note: A bibliophile is a lover of books.

b.note: A philanthropist loves mankind and helps others.

c.note: Illegible means that which cannot be read.
